params.body:
On a test by question, only the first line score entered on a page was saved. Every later one went to the server, got a 200, and was dropped, so the sum of its attainment level stayed "leeg". It showed on production with one attainment level on two questions (5 and 2 points, 3 and 1 entered: "op 7" with an empty sum), but having one level on several questions has nothing to do with it.

## Cause

Livewire 4 names a single cell in an update (`lineScores.<line>.<pupil>`) only when the map already holds that key. `lineScores` holds only the cells that have a score, so a cell that is still empty arrives as its whole line (`lineScores.<line>`) or as the whole map (`lineScores`), unless the map was empty too (`diffAndConsolidate` in livewire.esm.js). `Edit::updatedLineScores` took only `<line>.<pupil>` paths and returned on anything else.

Seen in headless Chromium on a seeded copy of that test:

- first entry: `{"lineScores.1.9": "3"}`, saved
- second entry: `{"lineScores": {"1": {"9": "3"}, "2": {"9": "1"}}}`, dropped
- on a page that already has scores, even the first new cell: `{"lineScores.1": {"6": "5", "9": "3"}}`, dropped

`QuestionTotals::derive` was right all along: it sums the lines once all of them are filled, and the second line never got there.

## Fix

- `updatingLineScores` keeps the map as the sheet held it before the update. `updatedLineScores` then saves every cell that differs (both sides read as `line.pupil` cells via `Arr::dot`), whatever path the browser used.
- Each cell goes through `saveLineScore`, with the same checks as a single cell before: the line belongs to this evaluation, may this user write, is the pupil absent, is it a number, is it within the line's points.
- A refused cell is reported at its own field and no longer holds back the others.
- A cell the browser did not change is not written, so it does not overwrite what someone else entered since the page opened.
- Rule R S3-9.14; R S3-9.12 now points to `saveLineScore`.

## Tests

`ATestByQuestionOnScreenTest::a_score_comes_through_whether_the_browser_sends_a_cell_a_line_or_the_sheet` sends the requests above: a named cell, then the whole map (sum 4), then a whole line. In one request it also has a refused cell next to a valid one, plus a cell that changed in the database meanwhile and must stay as it is. A line of another evaluation sent inside the whole map is still refused (403). The test fails on main at the second entry.

Seven mutations each turn a test red:
- only named cells taken (as before)
- every cell written, changed or not
- no snapshot before the update
- the first refusal stops the rest
- refusals not reported
- the line not checked
- the sum not shown again

In the browser the sum now shows 4 (and 7 for a second pupil entered as whole lines), also after a reload.

Pint and PHPStan are clean, and `bin/rules-sources.php` passes. Full suite on the workbench: 1382 passed, 20 failed. All 20 also fail on main there (build stamp, Chrome printing of reports); nothing new.

## Production data

The dropped scores were never stored, so no total is wrong: every sum matches the lines that were saved. What is missing is the entries themselves, and they can only be entered again once this is deployed. A read-only check across all evaluations by question on production found one, a test evaluation, with one pupil at 1 of 2 lines filled. Nothing else is affected.

The plain sheet's `updatedScores` has the same early return, but `$scores` holds every level and pupil from the start, so Livewire only sends a parent there when every child of a node changes in one request. Not touched here.
params.title: Save every line score the browser sends on a test by question
